author: blu
body: The frame is staged byte-by-byte into the kernel TX buffer (plain memory writes), then net-send-raw moves it to the NIC with a single REP OUTSW - one VM exit instead of one exit per byte. net-send-raw sends length divided by two words, therefore an odd-length frame is padded with one zero byte; the trailing pad is outside the IP total length and every receiver ignores it.
